title: When the Postcard Sings
premise: Sable Sandoval, a cellist whose hands froze mid-concert a year ago, returns to her coastal hometown for her grandmother's estate reading, where the family's music festival — and its fortune — hang on an inheritance clause she never knew existed. To deflect her relatives' scrutiny, she recruits Theo Marchetti, a charming festival stagehand and former conservatory dropout, to pose as her partner. As the fake romance deepens into something real, Sable discovers her grandmother's will ties the inheritance to whoever can revive the festival's dying tradition of the 'singing postcards' — recorded letters mailed between family members for three generations. When her uncle sabotages the recordings to claim the estate, Sable must perform again in front of everyone who witnessed her collapse; playing through her fear, she wins back not only the festival but the belief that timing is something you make, not wait for.
about_author: Astrid Sandoval is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian turned novelist who grew up above a sheet-music shop on the Oregon coast. Her stories explore how families pass down both instruments and wounds, one generation at a time.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A year after freezing mid-concert at Carnegie Hall, Sable teaches cello to disinterested teenagers and avoids her own instrument. An invitation to her grandmother's estate reading arrives with a postcard that plays a recording when opened. Emotional beat: dread laced with longing.

chapters.title: Saltwater Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She returns to Port Merrow and the crumbling seaside house where she learned cello. Her uncle Richard greets her like a rival, not family. The postcard's recording turns out to be her grandmother's voice: 'Bring someone who stays.' Emotional beat: unease beneath nostalgia.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Good Timing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Stagehand Theo Marchetti, hiding from his own failed conservatory past, overhears Sable rehearsing excuses about a nonexistent boyfriend. He offers himself up with disarming honesty. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Over coffee, they negotiate the fake relationship: no real feelings, gone after the reunion weekend. Theo asks only one thing — she teach him a song on cello. Emotional beat: playful contract masking mutual loneliness.

chapters.title: Arriving as a Couple
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They present themselves at the family dinner; Aunt Delia is delighted, Uncle Richard suspicious, cousin Priya openly skeptical. Sable performs happiness better than she ever performed Brahms. Emotional beat: performance anxiety in a new key.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The lawyer reveals the estate passes to whoever restores the festival and completes the archive of singing postcards within one summer. Richard produces his own claim. Sable realizes the fake boyfriend must now last a season. Emotional beat: shock hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Dessert Was Supposed to Be the End
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Walking home along the bluffs, their staged affection stops feeling staged; Theo catches himself meaning it. Sable pulls away, reminding him of the contract. Emotional beat: the first crack in the arrangement.

chapters.title: Postcards from the Attic
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sorting the attic, they find decades of postcards — her grandmother's courtship, quarrels, reconciliations, all sung aloud onto tape. Sable hears her grandmother young and afraid, just like her. Emotional beat: grief turning tender.

chapters.title: Lessons at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sable teaches him cello on the beach at dawn; his hands are clumsy but fearless, hers precise but terrified. Watching him fail joyfully, she envies him. Emotional beat: envy curdling into attraction.

chapters.title: Richard's Counterplay
chapters.summary: Richard's POV. Richard courts the town council to rezone the festival grounds for condos, framing it as saving the family from ruin. He dismisses the postcards as sentiment. Emotional beat: ambition dressed as duty.

chapters.title: The Missing Reel
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The crucial 1968 postcard recording — the one proving the festival's founding promise — is missing from the archive. Someone has been in the attic. Suspicion falls inward. Emotional beat: betrayal entering the house.

chapters.title: Rain on the Bandstand
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Storm traps them under the bandstand; Theo confesses he didn't drop out of conservatory — he was expelled for plagiarism he didn't commit and stopped fighting it. Sable holds his hand without a script. Emotional beat: vulnerability exchanged like keys.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. After the festival's first chaotic planning meeting, they nearly kiss in the boathouse; Sable retreats, terrified that wanting anything guarantees losing it. Theo leaves before the last train — deliberately missing it, then pretending he didn't. Emotional beat: desire colliding with self-protection.

chapters.title: Priya Knows
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Sable: she saw the contract notes in Theo's jacket. She offers silence in exchange for Sable finally being honest — with everyone, including herself. Emotional beat: exposure as reluctant mercy.

chapters.title: The Sabotage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The archive tapes are found water-damaged; Richard's fingerprints are metaphorically everywhere. Theo takes the blame publicly to protect Sable's standing, deepening the rift Priya exposed. Emotional beat: sacrifice mistaken for confirmation of deceit.

chapters.title: What the Postcard Sang
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Restoring a warped tape, Sable discovers the 1968 recording hidden inside a music box: her grandmother confessing she once froze on this same stage, and built the festival so no musician would be alone in failure. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as permission.

chapters.title: Confrontation at High Tide
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Sable faces Richard with the evidence; he breaks down, admitting fear, not greed, drove him — he was told his whole life he had no gift. The family fractures and regroups. Emotional beat: anger dissolving into shared damage.

chapters.title: Broken Strings
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Believing Sable chose the inheritance over him, Theo packs to leave for good. Sable finds his train ticket and the unfinished song he asked her to teach him, transcribed in his handwriting. Emotional beat: misunderstanding at its peak.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She runs to the station and asks him to stay — not as a contract, not until dessert, but past every deadline. He steps off the train. Emotional beat: the confession both were too proud to make.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The family rebuilds the bandstand together; Richard offers restitution, Priya runs logistics, Theo rigs the lights. Sable agrees to play the opening piece — her first performance since Carnegie. Emotional beat: terror transformed into readiness.

chapters.title: When the Postcard Sings
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Before the whole town, Sable plays through the place where she once froze, weaving in the melody from her grandmother's postcards while the restored recordings sing overhead. Her hands do not shake. Emotional beat: triumph earned through surrender, not control.

chapters.title: Someone Who Stays
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. The estate passes to Sable and the family collectively; the festival reopens with a new tradition — anyone may mail a singing postcard. On the empty beach, Theo asks what happens next. Sable answers: everything, starting now. Emotional beat: quiet, unguarded hope.
